headless testbench. A re-swap for more measurements is **not** the plan.
The i9 stays here (work computer). The 2080 is enough for everything except

<!-- SUPERSEDED-BY: Correction #3 | SCOPE: full | Arms inverted. 11-12 s is host 0.32.12, not docker. Also cites a re-check run that exists in no fixture. Do not quote. -->

**Do not compare the bench to 11–12 s for `gemma4:26b` on `constant-and-callers`.
Use 15–16 s.**

This document correctly flags (line 74) that `225` vs `211` decode is host ollama
**0.32.12** against docker **0.32.15**. But the snapshot then pairs **decode from
the host arm** with **wall clock from the docker arm**. Those are different
configurations and cannot be quoted together.

Measured on the host path (`pi` → `:11434`, ollama 0.32.12,
`gemma4-26b-e9pin-ctx16384-t0p8`), warm trials only, two independent runs:

| run | warm trials | mean |
|---|---|---:|
| `preswap-wallclock-2026-09-05` | 14.9 / 15.0 / 15.1 | **15.0 s** |
| re-check, same box, later | 15.5 / 15.8 / 16.0 | **15.8 s** |

**Reproducible at 15–16 s.** Cold trial 1 is unstable across the two runs (15.8 s
vs 28.9 s) and must not be averaged in.

The `:11435` docker daemon that produced 11–12 s is no longer running, so that
arm is not currently reproducible. **The testbench runs ollama 0.32.12**, matching
the host arm — so the like-for-like comparison is against 15–16 s. Quoting 11–12 s
would make an unchanged bench look ~25% slower and get charged to the i3.

**Reference pair for `gemma4:26b`, both from the 0.32.12 host path:**

| metric | value | source |
|---|---|---|
| decode | **226 tok/s** (224.4–229.0) | `preswap-baseline-2026-09-05` |

| csv-summarize-repair, warm | **46.0 s** (37.7–60.5) | same |

The document's core argument is unaffected and stands: **3090 + i9 is the
combination that cannot be bought back**, post-swap decode may match while
agentic wall clock will carry the i3, and `133` must not be cited. Only the
wall-clock figure needed the arm corrected.

**Version discipline going forward:** record the ollama version alongside every
wall-clock number. A 0.32.12/0.32.15 difference moves this metric ~25% — larger
than the CPU change the swap is meant to measure.

| | band | charge a delta only if |

The testbench is 0.32.12, so it matches the host daemon, not docker. A bench

## New finding 2026-09-07 — L0 is broken as authored, and it reaches outside the fixture

**Not a correction to #1–#4. New material.**

### What happened

An L0 battery was launched to break the L2 tie between `qwen3.8:27b`,
`qwen3.6:35b` and `gpt-oss:120b` (rationale: L2 saturates at 100% for all three,
so the tie had never been tested at a rung where the model must decide *what* to
do). It was stopped at 46/54 cells because it was generating repeated **sudo
password prompts on the operator's desktop**.

Cause, from the sudo audit trail:

```
PWD=/tmp/local-lane-eval-strict-log-format-L0-lcnc44ay
COMMAND=/usr/sbin/grep -iE \b(error|warning|critical)\b /var/log/messages-20260830
COMMAND=/usr/sbin/test -r /var/log/messages
COMMAND=/usr/sbin/head -5 /var/log/messages-20260906
```

`strict-log-format` at L0 reads:

> *"I need a summary of how many errors happened each hour from my logs."*

Its L2 prompt is about implementing `error_report(log_text)` in `src/logsum.py`
against `tests/check_logsum.py`. **The L0 prompt never names the artifact**, so
models reasonably read "my logs" as the host's real system logs, go to
`/var/log/messages` with sudo, never touch `src/logsum.py`, and fail the
postcondition.

### Three consequences

1. **All existing L0 data is invalid as a capability measure.** The corpus holds
   13 L0 trials against 2,659 total, at 2/13. That is not a floor effect and not
   a capability signal — it is prompt ambiguity. Do not cite it.

2. **Trials are not confined to their fixture directory.** They run in
   `/tmp/local-lane-eval-*` but nothing restricts them there. At L0 a model went
   to `/var/log` under sudo and could have gone anywhere sudo permits. This is
   invisible at L2 only because L2 hands the model exact paths. **This is a
   blast-radius property of the harness, not of the task**, and it applies to any
   goal-shaped prompt.

3. **"Just run L0" is not available as a tiebreaker.** The tasks are not authored
   for it. L0 prompts would need to name their artifact without re-specifying the
   procedure, and graders would need to accept correct-but-different solutions
   rather than one specified edit.

### Where that leaves the quality axis

Worse than it looked yesterday, and this is the load-bearing point for anyone
picking up the ranking:

| rung | state |
|---|---|
| **L2** | saturated — `qwen3.8:27b`, `qwen3.6:35b`, `gpt-oss:120b` all 100% clean |
| **L1** | near-saturated — three models 18/18; only `gemma4:26b` separates at 60.4% |
| **L0** | broken as authored (above) |

All three named batteries (`/54` seat, `/30`, `/18`) score **at L2 only**. The
library holds 17 tasks × 3 levels = 51 possible cells; the scored slice is 3
tasks at the single easiest rung.

**Recommendation: stop adding rounds.** Several have been run and each came back
tied, because more trials cannot separate models whose true rate is at the
ceiling. The next useful move is task work, not measurement — either repair the
L0 prompts and graders, or admit the two never-run library tasks
(`tool-forbidden`, `extraction-faithful`) which currently **fail prompt
validation** and so have never executed. `tool-forbidden` is notable: a task
about *declining* to act is not expressible as a numbered procedure, and the
linter requires L2 prompts to be plan-shaped (R3, numbered steps).

### Still-valid work from this session

- Speed axis re-measured and the protocol amended to use **task wall clock**
  instead of decode (`docs/LOCAL_LANE_POWER_RANKING_PROTOCOL.md`, amendment
  2026-09-06). Ranking at `docs/domain_runs/MODEL-RANKING-002-PRESWAP/RANKING.md`.
- `qwen3.6:35b` 51/51 and `gpt-oss:120b` 60/60 clean at L2 — both newly admitted.
- **Seat decision (operator):** `qwen3.8:27b` holds the seat; `qwen3.6:35b` is not
  eligible for it. Recorded as an operator judgement on dense-vs-MoE from
  interactive experience. Note the data does not support MoE-as-a-class being
  verbose: `qwen3.6:35b` (MoE, 1,858 tok) and `gpt-oss:120b` (MoE, 1,862) are
  both more economical than `gemma4:31b` (dense, 5,063).
- `verify_ranking_2026-09-06.py` re-derives the seat counts, exclusion rules and
  speed figures from traces and exits non-zero on failure.

## Correction 2026-09-07 (second) — the 11–12 s vs 15–16 s gap was the LEDGER, not the ollama version

**This supersedes the "Correction 2026-09-06 — the 11–12 s wall clock is from the
other arm" section above. That correction was wrong.**

It attributed the gap to host ollama 0.32.12 vs docker 0.32.15. Both arms were in
fact **host 0.32.12**, and the docker arm was *faster* still (6.0–10.9 s). The
real cause is `runner.py`'s timing window.

**`wall_clock_s` included ledger overhead.** At `runner.py:642`,
`start = time.monotonic()` fired *before* `_ledger_session_start`, which shells
out to the `operator` CLI (two `subprocess.run` calls, 15 s timeout each). Runs
passing `--no-ledger` skipped it; runs without the flag carried it.

Measured back to back, same cell, same machine, same tag:

| | trial 2 | trial 3 |
|---|---:|---:|
| with ledger | 15.7 s | 16.1 s |
| `--no-ledger` | 11.4 s | 10.0 s |

**~+4.5 s per trial** — a *fixed* cost on a *variable* quantity, so it inflated an
11 s task by 40% and a 46 s task by 10% and did **not** cancel in a ratio.
`wall_clock_s` is the power ranking's speed axis, so this contaminated the
published ranking.

**Fixed at source** (`runner.py`, 2026-09-07): the clock now starts *after* the
ledger call, so the measurement no longer depends on remembering a flag.
`_ledger_session_end` was already outside the window.

**Affected runs** — every wall-clock figure not taken with `--no-ledger`:
`roster-walltime-2026-09-05`, `preswap-wallclock-2026-09-05`,
`testbench-2080-e9-batch1`, `z13-wallclock-2026-09-07`. Corrected replacements:
`preswap-wallclock-noledger-2026-09-07` (desktop, done) and
`z13-wallclock-noledger-2026-09-07` (running).

**Credit:** Codex's `preswap-char-2026-09-06` fixture surfaced this. It happened
to pass `--no-ledger`, which is why its numbers disagreed with mine, and chasing
that disagreement found the bug.

**A caution the corrected data added.** Re-measuring the full grid showed the
deltas are *not* a constant −4.5 s; they span −40.1 to +18.4, because run-to-run
variance is far larger than the ledger effect. Within-cell spreads at n=3 run
**1.2x to 4.2x**. An earlier claim in this session that warm trials sit within
±3% was generalised from a single cell and is wrong. **Wall clock at n=3 cannot
order adjacent models** — the corrected ranking separates `qwen3.6:35b` clearly
and leaves the middle unresolved.

## Operator context sizing — measured 2026-09-08, supersedes the co-residency recommendation

**Recommendation: pin `num_ctx` to 131072 for interactive work. Do not pursue
two-model co-residency.** An earlier recommendation in this session to pin both
models to 32768 so they co-reside was **wrong for this workload** and is
withdrawn below.

### The operator's real context distribution

From 293 turns in `journalctl -u ollama` (`tokens: text = N` at slot init):

| | |
|---|---|
| median | **72,113 tokens** |
| max | **110,671** |
| turns over 32,768 | **191 / 293 — 65%** |
| turns over 65,536 | 156 / 293 — 53% |
| turns over 98,304 | 39 / 293 — 13% |

### Why co-residency is withdrawn

Both models *do* co-reside on the pair up to `num_ctx` 32768, with switching at
**0.6 s against 124 s** (`fixtures/coresidency-ceiling-2026-09-08`). That result
stands and is real.

**It is also unusable here.** At 32768, **65% of this operator's turns would be
truncated** — conversation history silently dropped mid-session on the majority
of turns. That is a worse failure than a slow switch, and unlike a slow switch it
does not announce itself. Co-residency is the right answer for a workload that
fits inside 32k; this one does not.

### What to do instead

| allocated | 27b resident | vs default |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 262,144 (ollama default) | 38,884 MiB | — |
| **131,072 (recommended)** | **28,620 MiB** | **−10,264 MiB** |
| 98,304 | 26,060 MiB | −12,824 MiB, but truncates 13% of turns |

131072 covers the observed maximum with headroom, saves ~10 GB against the
default, and loads faster. Both models still cannot co-reside at that depth
(28.6 + 32.4 GB against a 49.1 GB pool), so switching still costs a reload —
but from a clean state that is **~12–20 s**, not the 124 s measured while three
models were contending.

**Do not leave it unpinned.** The 262144 default pays full price for headroom
never reached: ~39 GB for one model, which forces an eviction on every switch and
leaves no room for anything else on the box.

### Supporting measurements

- `fixtures/hw-standard-preswap/` — single-card vs dual, enforced one-card via
  `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0` **plus `OLLAMA_LLM_LIBRARY=cuda_v13`** (the second is
  required; CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES does not hide a card from Vulkan).
- `fixtures/coresidency-ceiling-2026-09-08/` — the 32768 ceiling and the 0.6 s
  switch.
- `hw_standard.py` + `HW_STANDARD_PREDICTIONS.md` — the repeatable protocol and
  the predictions registered before it ran.

### Two results from those runs worth carrying forward

**Degradation is architecture-dependent, and the sign flips with the kind of
pressure.** Under *capacity* pressure (one card, fat context) the dense model
collapses — `qwen3.8:27b` at 262144 on a single card falls to **5.2 tok/s**, a
91% loss, while `qwen3.6:35b` degrades gracefully to 71.5. Under *sharing*
pressure (two models co-resident) it reverses — 35b loses 17% from 16k to 32k
while 27b is flat. Capacity pressure punishes dense; sharing pressure punishes
MoE.

**Ollama fits models to the available pool, not to the request.** With two models
resident, total memory was flat at ~43,650 MiB across 16k/24k/32k while only the
split between them moved. `num_ctx` does not mean the same thing on a shared box
as it does alone. Every prior measurement in this program was single-model, so
this had never been visible.

## Experiment 2026-09-08 - 27b single-card context sweep: spillover, fit boundary, and the headroom hypothesis

**Registered before running.** Predictions below are recorded first so the result
cannot be read back onto them.

### Why

Three open questions collapse into one measurement.

1. **Spillover is not characterised for the seat model.** The only offload curve in
   the program is `gemma4:26b` (31 layers, 4.45 ms/token empty): 224.8 tok/s at
   31/31 layers, **172.7 at 30/31**. One layer off the GPU costs 23%. Whether that
   transfers to a 66-layer model at 16 ms/token is unknown.
2. **The fit boundary is unknown.** Split allocation puts 27b at 24,933 MiB at
   ctx65536 against a 24,576 MiB card, but split carries 1,375-1,494 MiB of
   overhead that a solo allocation does not pay. The card also holds 360 MiB of
   display. Nobody has measured solo VRAM above ctx16384.
3. **The prefill result needs a mechanism.** In `singlecard-rank` (2026-09-08),
   dual prefilled faster than solo for `gemma4:31b` (-40%) and `qwen3.6:35b`
   (-19%), and made no difference for `qwen3.8:27b` or `gemma4:26b`. The penalty
   tracked **headroom**, not model size or architecture: the two models with under
   2.5 GB free on the card paid it, the two with over 5 GB free did not.

### Method

`hw_standard.py --models qwen3.8:27b --ctx 16384 32768 65536 131072`, solo host
`127.0.0.1:11435` (pinned with `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0` **and**
`OLLAMA_LLM_LIBRARY=cuda_v13`), dual host on `:11434`. Standard A, as-shipped
defaults, `draft_num_predict 4`. Loaded regime, ~12.8k prompt tokens.

### Predictions

| # | Prediction | Falsifier |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | 27b fits one card at 16384 and 32768. At 65536 it **fits with under 700 MiB spare** (24,933 minus ~1,400 split overhead plus 360 display). At 131072 it does not fit. | Any of those three outcomes differing |
| P2 | Prefill time per prompt token **rises materially at 65536** even while fully resident, because activation buffers get squeezed as headroom falls under ~700 MiB | Prefill per token flat from 16384 through 65536 |
| P3 | Decode stays within +/-10% from 16384 to 65536 while resident, then falls sharply once layers move to CPU | Decode declining steadily with context while still 66/66 on GPU |
| P4 | Spill costs 27b roughly **8% per CPU-resident layer**, not the 23% measured on 26b, because the fixed per-layer CPU cost (~1.3 ms) sits against a 3.6x slower baseline | 27b losing more than 15% per spilled layer |
| P5 | Ollama does not silently spill: an over-capacity config either fails to allocate or reports fewer than 66/66 layers | A row reporting 66/66 with VRAM above card capacity |

P2 is the one worth attacking. It is the only prediction that carries a proposed
mechanism, and the headroom pattern it rests on is n=4 with two models on each
side.

### Results

Pending. To be appended below by the same session, with predictions marked hit or
missed individually.

### Results 2026-09-08

`hw_standard.py`, Standard A, ~12.8k prompt tokens, n=3.

| config | decode tok/s | prefill ms/token | VRAM total | per card |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| dual ctx16384 | 62.8 | 0.865 | 20,424 | 10,293 / 10,131 |
| dual ctx32768 | 60.5 | 0.872 | 21,896 | 10,933 / 10,963 |
| dual ctx65536 | 60.8 | 0.872 | 24,844 | 12,215 / 12,629 |
| dual ctx131072 | 61.4 | 0.888 | 28,644 | 14,091 / 14,553 |
| solo ctx16384 | 55.1 | 0.872 | 18,907 | 18,907 / 0 |
| solo ctx32768 | 57.8 | 0.872 | 20,027 | 20,027 / 0 |
| solo ctx65536 | 56.4 | 0.872 | 22,237 | 22,237 / 0 |
| **solo ctx131072** | **11.2** | **1.573** | 22,823 | 22,823 / 0 |

### Predictions scored

**P1 - MISSED on both halves.** 27b fits one card at 65536 with **1,979 MiB spare**
(22,237 against 24,576 less 360 MiB display), not the under-700 predicted. The
error was arithmetic: solo runs 2,607 MiB lighter than dual at that depth, not the
1,375-1,494 MiB of split overhead assumed. At 131072 it also did not fail to
allocate as predicted. It loaded and spilled.

**P2 - FALSIFIED, cleanly, by its own stated falsifier.** Solo prefill is
**0.872 ms/token at 16384, 32768 and 65536** - dead flat while headroom fell from
5,669 to 1,979 MiB. Prefill rises only at 131072 (1.573), and that is spill, not
squeezed activation buffers. **The headroom hypothesis for the prefill penalty is
dead.** Whatever made `gemma4:31b` prefill 40% slower on one card in
`singlecard-rank`, it is not proximity to card capacity. That result is now an
unexplained finding again and should be labelled as one.

**P3 - HIT.** Solo decode 55.1 / 57.8 / 56.4 across 16k to 64k, inside +/-5%,
then collapses to 11.2 once spilled. Decode is flat with context while resident
and falls off a cliff when it is not.

**P4 - MISSED, badly, in the expensive direction.** Solo at 131072 holds 22,823
MiB against the 28,644 the model needs, so roughly 5,821 MiB (~20%, about 13 of 66
layers) sits on CPU. Time per token goes 17.7 ms to 89.3 ms, so **~5.5 ms per
CPU-resident layer**, four times the ~1.3 ms measured on `gemma4:26b`. The
predicted 8% per layer is actually ~31%, past the 15% falsifier. **Per-layer spill
cost does not transfer between models.** Caveat: the layer count is inferred from
the VRAM shortfall, not measured, because of the instrument gap below.

**P5 - the instrument cannot answer it.** Every solo row reports `layers: None`.
`hw_standard.py` does not capture layer placement on the solo daemon, so the
ctx131072 row records `status: ok` with no indication that a fifth of the model
is on CPU. Only the VRAM shortfall and the 5x throughput drop reveal it. **This is
a fail-closed gap in a tool written to be fail-closed** and should be fixed before
the tool is used on the testbench, where placement questions are the whole point.

### The finding that matters for the card decision

At **ctx131072**, the depth the operator sizing section recommends for interactive
work, dual runs **61.4 tok/s** and solo runs **11.2**. That is **5.5x**, and it is
the first measurement in this program where the second card earns its place on
throughput rather than capacity alone.

Read alongside the null: splitting does not help decode when the model fits one
card, and is worth 5.5x when it does not. The second card is not a speed upgrade.
It is what keeps the seat model resident at the operator's real context depth.

## Proposed experiment - what makes dual prefill faster for some models and not others

**Proposed 2026-09-08, not yet run.** Registered before execution.

### The open finding

`singlecard-rank-2026-09-08` measured a real dual-card prefill advantage for two
of four models, and the proposed mechanism was falsified the same evening.

| model | layers | architecture | class | solo prefill ms/token | dual advantage |
|---|---:|---|---|---:|---:|
| `gemma4:26b` | 31 | gemma4 | dense | 0.239 | n/a, single-card in both arms |
| `qwen3.6:35b` | 42 | qwen35moe | MoE | 0.374 | **19%** |
| `qwen3.8:27b` | 66 | qwen35 | dense | 0.865 | none |
| `gemma4:31b` | 61 | gemma4 | dense | 0.971 | **40%** |

The headroom hypothesis is dead: 27b prefill is flat at 0.872 ms/token from
ctx16384 to ctx65536 while headroom falls from 5,669 to 1,979 MiB
(`ctx-sweep-27b-2026-09-08`).

The remaining candidates do not separate cleanly on this data. Layer count fails
(61 and 42 benefit, 66 does not). Architecture family fails (gemma4 31b benefits,
qwen 35b benefits, qwen 27b does not). Dense versus MoE fails (dense 31b benefits,
dense 27b does not). **Four models is not enough to distinguish them, and adding
models will not help if the wrong variable is being varied.**

### Design: vary prompt length, not model count

`hw_standard.py` already carries `--depth-mult` (corpus repeats, 1 is ~12.8k
prompt tokens). Sweeping it separates mechanism classes directly, because the
shape of the advantage against prompt length is diagnostic:

- **Constant in seconds** across depths means a fixed per-load setup cost, not
  per-token work. Scheduling or allocation, not bandwidth.
- **Constant in ms per token** means genuine per-token processing, and two cards
  are contributing something during prefill that they do not during decode.
- **Growing faster than linear** means a capacity effect appearing as the
  activation working set grows.

Method: `--models gemma4:31b qwen3.8:27b --depth-mult 1 2 4 --ctx 65536`, both
arms, solo daemon verified per 2b.2. 31b is the largest observed effect, 27b is
the null control. Twelve configurations.

### Predictions

| # | Prediction | Falsifier |
|---|---|---|
| Q1 | The 31b dual advantage is **constant in ms per token**, within +/-20% across depth-mult 1, 2 and 4 | The advantage in seconds is flat while ms/token falls, or it grows superlinearly |
| Q2 | 27b shows **no dual prefill advantage at any depth**, holding its null | 27b develops an advantage above depth-mult 1 |
| Q3 | Solo prefill ms/token for both models is **flat across depth-mult**, as it was flat across `num_ctx` in the 27b sweep | Either model's solo prefill per token rises with prompt length while resident |
| Q4 | Decode is **unaffected by depth-mult** for both models on both arms, since it is flat across `num_ctx` while resident | Decode moving with prompt length at fixed context |

Q1 is the load-bearing one. If it holds, prefill genuinely uses both cards and
decode does not, which would be the first asymmetry of that kind in this program.
If the advantage turns out to be constant in seconds, the effect is setup cost and
has nothing to do with prefill at all - in which case the `singlecard-rank`
prefill column is measuring load behaviour and should be relabelled.

**Do not add more models until this is run.** The instinct to widen the roster is
what produced four models and no mechanism.
